pairing.findOnNetwork: Find it on your network — no reset needed
pairing.findOnNetworkA11y: Add an air conditioner from your network
pairing.findOnNetworkHint: Finds units already connected to this Wi-Fi
pairing.discoverEmptyDesc: Nothing on this Wi-Fi answered the scan. Run through the checks below — it is usually one of the first two.
pairing.searchedNetwork: Searched your network at {{network}} — if that isn’t your home Wi-Fi, switch networks and scan again.
pairing.scanBlockedTitle: Climate King can’t reach this network
pairing.scanBlockedDesc: The scan never left your phone. Allow Climate King to find devices on your local network, then try again.
pairing.checkPowered: The air conditioner is powered on. A unit on standby still answers; one switched off at the breaker doesn’t.
pairing.checkSameNetwork: This phone is on the same Wi-Fi as the unit — the 2.4 GHz band, not a guest network, and with no VPN running.
pairing.checkPermission: Climate King is allowed to find devices on your local network (Settings › Climate King › Local Network).
pairing.checkIsolation: Your router isn’t separating devices from each other — “AP isolation” or “client isolation” hides the AC from your phone.
pairing.neverConnectedDesc: Then it can’t appear here. A unit that has never been online has to be set up once, step by step — about two minutes.
pairing.setUpFromScratch: Set it up step by step
pairing.neverConnectedDescNoModel: Then it can’t appear here. Choose your model first and we’ll walk you through the one-time setup — about two minutes.
pairing.pickYourModel: Choose your model to get started
pairing.pairHint: Pairs this air conditioner with the app
pairing.alreadyAddedHint: Tap a unit that is already added to pair it again and move it to the home you are in.
pairing.readdHint: Pairs this air conditioner again and moves it to the home you are in
pairing.beforeYouStartDesc: Pairing puts your AC on your home network. Here’s what it needs.
pairing.setupNeedsPermissionBody: Climate King needs {{permissions}} access to find your air conditioner.
pairing.accessDeclined: Access was declined, so it can only be turned back on from your phone’s settings.
pairing.permLocationHint: Android requires it to see nearby Wi-Fi networks — including your air conditioner’s setup network.
pairing.permLocalNetworkHint: Android 16 and later require it before the app can reach your air conditioner over Wi-Fi.
pairing.yourAcDesc: Power the unit on and reset its Wi-Fi module — you should hear a beep. Then pick the matching appliance type from the list.
pairing.yourNetworkDesc: Keep Wi-Fi and Location switched on, and have your 2.4 GHz network name and password to hand — most air conditioners can’t join 5 GHz.
pairing.resetTip: The Wi-Fi module only releases its hotspot about 2 minutes after it is reset.
pairing.wifiPickerBody: Pick the network your air conditioner should join.
pairing.wifiPickerEmpty: No networks found nearby. Type the name instead.
pairing.wifi5GhzOnly: 5 GHz only — the air conditioner can’t join this one
pairing.wifiDifferentNetwork: Your phone is on {{phone}}. Connect it to {{chosen}} before finishing — an air conditioner can only be controlled from the same network.
pairing.wifi24GhzHint: It must be a 2.4 GHz network — air conditioners can’t join 5 GHz. If your router shows one name for both, that’s fine.
pairing.wifiOverBluetooth: Keep Bluetooth on and stay near the air conditioner — Climate King connects to it directly to set it up.
pairing.wifiManualJoin: Before you tap Connect, open your phone’s Wi‑Fi settings and join the air conditioner’s own network — its name starts with “GR-” or is a short code of letters and numbers. If it asks for a password, enter {{password}}. Then come back here without closing this screen.
pairing.provisionConfirming: Waiting for it to join your network
pairing.provisionSlow: This takes up to a minute — the unit restarts onto your Wi-Fi before it answers.
pairing.provisionTipPassword: Check the Wi-Fi password character by character — one wrong letter is by far the most common cause, and the unit can’t tell you which.
pairing.provisionTipBand: The network has to be 2.4 GHz. If your router gives both bands the same name, split them for a few minutes while you set the unit up.
pairing.provisionTipSecurity: Hidden networks and WPA3-only security are refused by these modules. Switch to a visible WPA2 network to get through setup.
pairing.provisionTipHotspot: Still stuck? Share a 2.4 GHz hotspot from another phone and set the unit up on that — if it joins, the module is fine and your router is the thing to look at.
pairing.provisionFixDesc: Change anything that looks wrong and try again — you don’t need to start over.
pairing.provisionRejoinDesc: Your phone is back on your normal Wi-Fi now. Rejoin the air conditioner’s own network first, or the retry has no way to reach it.
pairing.resetRemoteSubtitle: Hold the remote controller and point it at the appliance.
pairing.resetRemoteStep1: Use the remote controller to turn off the air conditioner.
pairing.resetRemoteStep2: Press “Mode” and “WiFi” together until you hear a beep — that means the reset succeeded.
pairing.resetPanelSubtitle: Use the buttons on the indoor unit panel.
pairing.resetPanelStep1: Power on the air conditioner at the indoor unit.
pairing.resetPanelStep2: Press and hold “Health” + “Sleep” for about 5 seconds until you hear a beep.
pairing.resetRvStep1: Use the remote controller to turn off the air conditioner.
pairing.resetRvStep2: Check that “WiFi” shows on the remote’s display. If it doesn’t, press “Mode” and “LED / TURBO” together once to switch it on.
pairing.resetRvStep3: Point the remote at the unit and hold “Mode” and “LED / TURBO” together for about 10 seconds, until you hear a beep. On a remote with a “WiFi” button, hold “Mode” and “WiFi” instead.
pairing.resetRvTip: About 2 minutes after the reset, the unit opens its own Wi‑Fi network — named with a short code of letters and numbers, like 1ef6d89c.
pairing.notFoundDefault: We couldn’t find a device to pair. Run through these checks, then try again.
pairing.tipPoweredOn: Make sure the air conditioner is powered on.
pairing.tipModuleReset: Confirm the Wi-Fi module was reset — you should have heard a beep.
pairing.tipStayClose: Stay close to the AC and your Wi-Fi router during setup.
pairing.tipUse24Ghz: Use a 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi network (smart modules don’t join 5 GHz).
pairing.tipSameNetwork: Keep this phone on the same Wi-Fi as the unit — not a guest network.
pairing.tipAlreadyPaired: A unit already paired with another app won’t issue a second key.
pairing.tipResetThenScan: Reset the Wi-Fi module (hold Mode + Fan on the remote until it beeps), then scan again.
pairing.slowSameNetwork: Taking longer than usual? Make sure this phone is on the same Wi‑Fi network as the air conditioner — not a guest network.
pairing.slowHotspot: Taking longer than usual? Some units release their hotspot about 2 minutes after a reset — keep waiting.
pairing.connectedAndReady: {{name}} is connected and ready to control.
pairing.tryHotspotSetup: Set up through the unit’s own Wi‑Fi
pairing.shareSetupReport: Share a setup report with support
pairing.discoverIntro: Air conditioners already connected to this Wi-Fi appear here. Make sure your phone is on the same network as the unit — not a guest network.
pairing.wifiIntro: Enter the Wi-Fi your air conditioner should join — the one this phone uses at home.
pairing.catalogEmptyDesc: We couldn’t load the list of supported units. Pull to retry, or add an air conditioner already on your Wi-Fi.
pairing.findIntro: After the reset, the air conditioner opens a setup network of its own. Keep this screen open — it will appear here by itself.
pairing.findFoundDesc: Tap Connect on the one you just reset.
pairing.findSearching: Searching for air conditioners in setup mode…
pairing.findSlow: Still nothing? Some units take up to 2 minutes to open their setup network. If it has been longer than that, reset the unit’s Wi-Fi again.
pairing.findNeedLocationTitle: Allow location to find your AC
pairing.findNeedLocationBody: Android only lets apps with location access see nearby Wi-Fi networks — your air conditioner’s included. Climate King never reads or stores where you are.
pairing.findWifiOffBody: Your phone’s Wi-Fi is off, so it can’t see the air conditioner. Switch it on and come back — the search picks up by itself.
pairing.findLocationOffBody: Android hides nearby Wi-Fi networks from every app while Location is off. Switch it on and come back — the search picks up by itself.
pairing.findNotListed: Not listed? Choose from all nearby networks
pairing.findPickerBody: Pick the network named after your unit — it usually starts with “GR-” or is a short code of letters and numbers.
pairing.signalWeak: Weak signal — move closer to the unit
pairing.nearbyReadyDesc: Found nearby in setup mode — no reset needed.
pairing.wifiHotspotWait: Just reset it? Its network can take up to 2 minutes to appear.
pairing.wifiUseHotspot: Does your unit open its own Wi‑Fi network? Set it up that way
pairing.wifiPasswordCheck: One wrong character is the most common reason setup fails — tap the eye to check it.
pairing.wifiPasswordRemembered: Filled in from the last time a unit joined this network.
pairing.wifiRemember: Remember this password on this phone
pairing.permNearbyHint: Android 12 and later require it to find air conditioners that set up over Bluetooth.

feedback.title: Feedback
feedback.clearMessage: This permanently removes all your submitted feedback. This can't be undone.
feedback.descriptionPlaceholder: Describe the problem you ran into, in detail
feedback.attachmentsMessage: Attach up to 4 screenshots or photos that show the problem. Clear images help us resolve your report faster.
feedback.submittedMessage: Thanks for the report — our team will take a look. You can track it under History.
feedback.oldOrdersMessage: No work orders from earlier app versions are linked to this account.
feedback.privacyNote: We use your details only to follow up on this report. Your information is kept private.

userResearch.title: User research
userResearch.emptyDesc: New surveys will appear here. Check back soon.
userResearch.completeBody: Thank you for helping us make Climate King better. Your feedback goes straight to the team.
userResearch.intro: Help shape Climate King. Your answers are anonymous and take just a couple of minutes.

lab.title: Lab Features
lab.followSystemDesc: Match your device's light or dark setting
lab.followSystemHint: Turn off “Follow the system” to choose a mode yourself.
lab.widgetStep1: Long-press a blank area of your home screen (or pinch with two fingers) to enter edit mode, then add the Climate King widget.
lab.widgetStep2: Follow the prompts on the widget to choose which device it controls.
lab.widgetIntro: View device status and control your AC straight from your phone's home screen. Tap the widget any time to jump back into the app.

permissions.photosDesc: Access images on your phone so you can pick and upload attachments.
permissions.cameraDesc: Scan QR codes for pairing and invites, and capture photos to upload.
permissions.localNetworkDesc: Talk to your air conditioner directly over your Wi-Fi, with no trip through the internet.
permissions.locationDesc: Find nearby Wi-Fi networks and devices for setup and energy services.
permissions.nearbyDevicesDesc: Find your air conditioner over Bluetooth when you set it up.

energyTips.setpointBody: Every 1°C warmer in cooling can cut that unit’s energy use by up to 5%. Try 24–25°C.
energyTips.topDeviceTitle: One unit is doing the heavy lifting
energyTips.topDeviceBody: Most of your usage comes from a single AC. A schedule or eco mode there saves the most.
energyTips.nightBody: A “Good Night” schedule that nudges the temperature up overnight trims hours of full-power cooling.
energyTips.autoBody: Auto mode matches output to the room and avoids overcooling — usually lighter on energy than a fixed low temperature.

scheduleTemplates.morningDesc: Cool the home on weekday mornings
scheduleTemplates.awayDesc: Turn everything off when you leave
scheduleTemplates.movieDesc: A cool, calm living room on demand

appliances.rv35Desc: RV & camper · Type I and Type II

remoteAccess.title: Remote access
remoteAccess.intro: Your air conditioner only answers on your home Wi‑Fi — it has no address of its own on the internet. To reach it while you are out, leave a small bridge program running on something at home.
remoteAccess.newBridgeSub: Name the machine that will stay switched on at home.
remoteAccess.emptyBody: Without one, your air conditioners only work while this phone is on the home Wi‑Fi.
remoteAccess.tokenBody: Save this now — it is shown once and cannot be recovered. The bridge at home signs in with it.
remoteAccess.tokenHint: Long‑press the token to copy it, or use Share to send it to the machine.
remoteAccess.removeBody: It stops working straight away. Your air conditioners keep working whenever this phone is on the home Wi‑Fi.
